name: Larry Williams 'Oops!' gap-down reversal, 2-day hold
rule: pl = bars[i-1].low. Oops bar at i: open[i] < pl (opened below yesterday's low) AND close[i] > pl (closed back above it). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat. holdBars = 2 (exit at the close of bar i+2). No other filter. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Williams' claim: an opening gap below the prior low that fails the same day traps emotional sellers; the forced reversal carries over 1-2 sessions.
source: Larry Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (Wiley 1999), ch. 'Oops!'; popular on YouTube/TradingView under the same name

name: Larry Williams bearish 'Smash Day' reversal buy, 3-day hold
rule: Smash day at bar j: close[j] < low[j-1] (closes below the prior day's low). Trigger at bar i = j+1: close[i] > high[j] (price takes out the smash day's high and holds into the close). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat. holdBars = 3. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: A close under the prior low then an immediate reclaim of the smash high is Williams' 'hidden smash day' setup: the breakdown failed, so trapped shorts have to cover.
source: Larry Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), ch. 'Smash Day Patterns'

name: Connors %b strategy: Bollinger %b < 0.2 three days running above the 200-day, exit %b > 0.8 (ETFs)
rule: mid = ctx.sma('close',20); sd = ctx.rollingStd('close',20); upper = mid+2sd; lower = mid-2sd; pb = (close-lower)/(upper-lower). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > ctx.sma('close',200,i) AND pb[i] < 0.2 AND pb[i-1] < 0.2 AND pb[i-2] < 0.2. EXIT when pb[i] > 0.8. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Connors' ETF variant of his short-term pullback rules: three closes near the lower band inside a long-term uptrend is an exhausted sell-off that reverts to the upper band.
source: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, High Probability ETF Trading (2009), '%b Strategy'

name: Connors RSI(2) < 10 above the 200 EMA on hourly crypto, exit RSI(2) > 65
rule: r = ctx.rsi(2); e = ctx.ema('close',200). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > e[i] AND r[i] < 10. EXIT when r[i] > 65 OR 24 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The most-copied retail mean-reversion rule applied where beginners actually run it (hourly BTC/alts); if the daily-stock edge is structural it should show up here too.
source: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), ch. 'The 2-period RSI'; countless 'RSI 2 crypto' YouTube videos

name: O'Neil sell rules: 52-week-high breakout on volume with a 7% stop and a 20% profit target
rule: hi = max(close over bars i-250..i-1). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > hi AND volume[i] > 1.5 * ctx.sma('volume',50,i-1). Record entry = close[i]. EXIT at the first close <= 0.93*entry (7% stop) OR close >= 1.20*entry (20% profit) OR 120 bars after entry (time stop). Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: O'Neil's 7-8% stop and 20-25% sell rule are the most quoted beginner risk rules; the test asks whether the asymmetric bracket adds anything to a plain new-high breakout.
source: William O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (4th ed 2009), ch. 10-11; Investors.com 'The 7%-8% sell rule'

name: O'Neil 50-day line: buy the first pullback that touches a rising 50-day SMA above the 200-day, sell 3% below it
rule: s50 = ctx.sma('close',50); s200 = ctx.sma('close',200). Uptrend: close[i] > s200[i] AND s50[i] > s50[i-10]. Clean approach: low[k] > s50[k] for every k in i-10..i-1 (first touch in 10 bars). Touch: low[i] <= 1.01*s50[i] AND close[i] > s50[i] AND close[i] > open[i]. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND all hold. EXIT when close[i] < 0.97*s50[i] OR 30 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: O'Neil/IBD teach buying leaders at the first test of the 50-day line; institutions defending their cost basis there is the stated mechanism.
source: William O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (2009), ch. 11 ('buy at the 50-day moving average'); IBD 'How to use the 50-day line'

name: Death cross as a contrarian buy: long the day the 50-day crosses below the 200-day, hold 60 bars
rule: s50 = ctx.sma('close',50); s200 = ctx.sma('close',200). Death cross at bar i: s50[i] < s200[i] AND s50[i-1] >= s200[i-1]. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat. holdBars = 60. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The widely repeated claim that the death cross is a lagging signal that marks lows rather than starts declines; buying it tests that claim directly.
source: Popularised by financial media each time the S&P prints one (e.g. Bloomberg/CNBC 'death cross is actually bullish' pieces, 2018-2022); Investopedia 'Death Cross'

name: Golden cross long with an RSI(14) overbought profit-take: out at RSI 75, back in at RSI 55 (equity ETFs)
rule: s50 = ctx.sma('close',50); s200 = ctx.sma('close',200); r = ctx.rsi(14). Regime: bull = s50[i] > s200[i]. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND bull AND r[i] <= 55. EXIT when NOT bull OR r[i] >= 75. (So after a profit-take the rule re-enters once RSI cools to 55 while the cross is intact.) Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Beginners are told to 'take profits when overbought'; this isolates whether an RSI profit-take improves a golden-cross hold or just sells the strongest part of the trend.
source: Investopedia 'Golden Cross' and 'RSI overbought'; TradingView 'Golden cross + RSI' scripts

name: 200-day SMA with a fixed 3% envelope (whipsaw filter): in above +3%, out below -3% (equity ETFs)
rule: s = ctx.sma('close',200). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > 1.03*s[i]. EXIT when close[i] < 0.97*s[i]. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The standard beginner fix for 200-day whipsaws is a percentage band; the question is whether the fewer trades pay for the later entries and exits.
source: Mebane Faber, 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation' (2007/2013) discussion of bands; Investopedia 'Moving average envelope'

name: Weinstein stage analysis on weekly bars: Stage 2 above a rising 30-week MA, exit only when price is below a flat-or-falling MA (Stage 4)
rule: W = ctx.resample(bars,'1w'); use only complete weeks. Decide only on the first daily bar after a week completes. m = SMA of the last 30 complete weekly closes; mPrev = the same SMA 4 weeks earlier; rising = m > mPrev. wc = last complete weekly close. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND wc > m AND rising. EXIT when wc < m AND NOT rising (Stage 4). Hold otherwise (a dip below a still-rising MA is Stage 2 noise). Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Weinstein's rule is a 30-week MA with a slope condition, which plain MA tests ignore; a flat MA is the 'topping' stage he says you sell into, not every cross.
source: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets (1988), ch. 2-3

name: Faber 10-month SMA timing on crypto: long when the monthly close is above the 10-month average, cash otherwise
rule: M = ctx.resample(bars,'1M'); use only complete months. Decide only on the first daily bar after a month completes. mc = last complete monthly close; avg = SMA of the last 10 complete monthly closes (need 10). ENTER long at close of that bar if flat AND mc > avg. EXIT at that bar if long AND mc <= avg. No decisions on other bars. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Faber's GTAA rule is the most-cited beginner timing model; crypto's deep bear years are exactly where a monthly trend filter is supposed to earn its keep.
source: Mebane Faber, 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation', Journal of Wealth Management (2007); r/CryptoCurrency and YouTube '10-month SMA crypto' posts

name: Turtle System 1 on US stocks: 20-day breakout taken only after a losing breakout, 55-day fail-safe, 2N stop, 10/20-day exits
rule: N = ctx.atr(20). S1 breakout at bar i: close[i] > max(high over i-20..i-1). S2 breakout: close[i] > max(high over i-55..i-1). Hypothetical tracker (per asset, independent of the real position; at most ONE open hypothetical trade at a time, an S1 breakout while one is open is ignored by the tracker): every S1 breakout opens a hypothetical trade at close[i] with stop = entry-2N and exit on the first close < min(low over k-10..k-1) or close < stop; its outcome is winner if the exit close > entry else loser; store lastOutcome when it completes. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND ((S1 breakout AND lastOutcome != winner) OR S2 breakout). Record entryType and stop = close[i]-2N. EXIT when close[i] < stop OR (entryType S1 AND close[i] < min(low over i-10..i-1)) OR (entryType S2 AND close[i] < min(low over i-20..i-1)). Long only, one unit, no pyramiding. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The real Turtle rules skip a 20-day breakout after a winning one and rely on the 55-day fail-safe; every public 'Turtle' test drops that filter, so beginners never see the rule as taught.
source: Curtis Faith, Way of the Turtle (2007), ch. 5 and 'The Original Turtle Trading Rules' (free PDF, 2003), System 1 entry filter
prereg_note: Clarified: one hypothetical S1 trade at a time (Turtle rule as published), so the last-breakout outcome is unambiguous.

name: Darvas box breakout on crypto: 3-day confirmed box top and bottom near a 100-day high, buy the top on 1.5x volume, stop under the box
rule: Box construction (causal): a top H at bar t is confirmed at bar t+3 when high[t+1..t+3] are all < high[t]; then the bottom L at bar u > t is confirmed at u+3 when low[u+1..u+3] are all > low[u] and no high in t+1..u+3 exceeds H; the box is [L,H] once both are confirmed; a later confirmed higher top restarts construction; if any high exceeds H before L is confirmed, H is discarded and construction restarts from the next confirmed top. A completed box is consumed by its first close above H or below L: the entry can fire only on that first close above H (if the volume or near-high test fails on that bar the box is void), and construction then restarts. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND a box exists AND close[i] > H AND volume[i] > 1.5*ctx.sma('volume',50,i-1) AND close[i] >= 0.97*max(high over i-100..i-1) (near the 100-day high, Darvas only bought near highs). Set stop = L. When a new box completes above the entry box while long, raise stop to its L. EXIT when close[i] < stop. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Darvas' box method is the original breakout-trailing system; crypto beginners apply it to alt breakouts, and it is only tested on stocks so far.
source: Nicolas Darvas, How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960); TradingView 'Darvas Box' built-in indicator
prereg_note: Clarified the box lifecycle: a completed box is used once (first close above H or below L consumes it); a high above H before L is confirmed discards the top. Trailing rule: stop rises to the L of any newer completed box only if that L is above the current stop.

name: Fixed 2:1 reward-to-risk bracket on a 20-day breakout above the 200-day: stop 2 ATR, target 4 ATR
rule: a = ctx.atr(14). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > max(high over i-20..i-1) AND close[i] > ctx.sma('close',200,i). entry = close[i]; stop = entry - 2*a[i]; target = entry + 4*a[i] (fixed at entry). EXIT at the first close <= stop OR close >= target OR 40 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: 'Always use at least 2:1 reward to risk' is the first rule in every beginner course; a fixed bracket on a plain breakout tests whether that exit geometry helps or caps the trend.
source: Van Tharp, Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom (1999) on R-multiples; Babypips / Investopedia 'Risk-reward ratio'

name: Breakout and retest: buy the first pullback to a broken 50-day high within 15 bars, stop 3% under the level
rule: Breakout at bar j: close[j] > L where L = max(high over j-50..j-1); remember L and j (latest breakout only). Evaluation order at bar i: first test the retest against the latest breakout (L, j) recorded on bars before i, then register bar i as a new breakout if close[i] > max(high over i-50..i-1). Retest trigger at bar i with j < i <= j+15: low[i] <= 1.02*L AND close[i] > L AND close[i] > open[i]. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat. EXIT when close[i] < 0.97*L OR 20 bars after entry. One trade per breakout. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: 'Wait for the retest' is the most common beginner breakout advice; it should cut the false-breakout cost if former resistance really turns into support.
source: Peter Brandt / classical charting (Schabacker 1932, Edwards & Magee 1948 'support becomes resistance'); YouTube 'break and retest strategy'
prereg_note: Clarified evaluation order: retest uses the latest breakout from bars before i; bar i may then register as a new breakout.

name: Stockbee 4% momentum burst: 4%+ up day on 1.5x volume, strong close, quiet prior 3 days, 5-day hold
rule: ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i]/close[i-1]-1 >= 0.04 AND volume[i] >= 1.5*ctx.sma('volume',50,i-1) AND close[i] >= low[i] + 0.75*(high[i]-low[i]) AND (high[i]-low[i]) > (high[i-1]-low[i-1]) AND |close[i-1]/close[i-4]-1| <= 0.03 (quiet 3-day run-up). EXIT when close[i] < low[entryBar] OR 5 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Bonde's claim: a range expansion out of a quiet base on volume marks the start of a 3-5 day momentum burst as swing traders pile in.
source: Pradeep Bonde (Stockbee), '4% breakout' / 'Momentum Burst' method, stockbee.blogspot.com (2010-)

name: Wyckoff spring: undercut of the 30-day low on sub-1.5x volume, close back inside within 3 bars, target the range top
rule: At bar s: L = min(low over s-30..s-1); spring if low[s] < L AND volume[s] < 1.5*ctx.sma('volume',50,s-1) (no supply); H = max(high over s-30..s-1). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND there is a spring bar s in {i-2,i-1,i} AND close[i] > L AND close[k] <= L for all k in s..i-1 (first close back inside) AND min(low over s..i) == low[s]. stop = low[s]; target = H. EXIT when close[i] < stop OR close[i] >= target OR 30 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Wyckoff's spring: a shakeout under support on light volume shows sellers are exhausted, and the return into the range starts the markup toward the range top.
source: Richard Wyckoff course (1931) as taught in Hank Pruden, The Three Skills of Top Trading (2007); StockCharts ChartSchool 'Wyckoff Method'

name: Bulkowski double bottom (Adam & Adam): two fractal lows within 3% at least 15 bars apart, 10% middle rise, buy the neckline break, measured-move target
rule: Pivot low at k confirmed at k+5: low[k] < low[k-5..k-1] and low[k] < low[k+1..k+5]. Pattern: the two most recent confirmed pivot lows a < b with 15 <= b-a <= 60, |low[b]/low[a]-1| <= 0.03, P = max(high over a..b) >= 1.10*min(low[a],low[b]). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND b+5 < i <= b+45 AND close[i] > P AND close[k] <= P for every k in b+1..i-1 (first close above the neckline). target = P + (P - min(low[a],low[b])); stop = low[b]. EXIT when close[i] >= target OR close[i] < stop OR 60 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Bulkowski reports the double bottom as one of the better-performing reversal patterns once the neckline breaks; this is the exact pattern definition from the book.
source: Thomas Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2nd ed 2005), 'Double Bottoms, Adam & Adam'; thepatternsite.com
prereg_note: Made "first close above the neckline" explicit: no close above P between b+1 and i-1.

name: Elder Triple Screen on daily stocks: weekly MACD histogram rising, daily 2-day Force Index dip, buy the break of the prior day's high
rule: W = ctx.resample(bars,'1w'), complete weeks only; weekly MACD(12,26,9) histogram h on weekly closes; tide = h[last] > h[prev]. e13 = ctx.ema('close',13); FI = EMA(2) of (close[k]-close[k-1])*volume[k]. ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND tide AND e13[i] > e13[i-1] AND FI[i-1] < 0 AND close[i] > high[i-1]. EXIT when NOT tide OR close[i] < e13[i] - ctx.atr(14,i) OR 20 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Elder's screens: trade only with the weekly tide, enter on a daily wave against it, trigger on the intraday ripple; tested here on the stocks the book is about rather than hourly crypto.
source: Alexander Elder, Trading for a Living (Wiley 1993), ch. 'Triple Screen Trading System'; Come Into My Trading Room (2002)

name: 'Gaps get filled': buy an unfilled 1%+ down gap at the close, exit when the pre-gap close is reclaimed or after 10 bars
rule: Gap down at bar i: open[i] < low[i-1] AND open[i] <= 0.99*close[i-1] AND close[i] < close[i-1] (still unfilled at the close). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat; fillLevel = close[i-1]. EXIT when close[k] >= fillLevel OR 10 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The retail belief that most gaps fill; the test prices it on single large caps with a defined fill target rather than on the index.
source: Investopedia 'Playing the Gap'; the 'gaps always get filled' rule across r/Daytrading and StockCharts ChartSchool 'Gaps'

name: Bottom fishing: buy a new 52-week closing low, hold 60 bars
rule: lo = min(close over bars i-250..i-1). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] < lo (new 52-week closing low). holdBars = 60. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Beginners ask whether blue chips at 52-week lows are bargains; the 52-week-high literature says no, but large-cap lows with a 3-month hold is the actual question.
source: Investopedia '52-Week High/Low'; George & Hwang (2004) for the high side; Barron's/Motley Fool 'buying stocks at 52-week lows' columns

name: Buy the 10% correction in equity ETFs, sell at the next 1-year high
rule: peak = max(close over i-252..i). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] <= 0.90*peak. EXIT when close[i] >= max(close over i-252..i-1) (new 1-year closing high) OR 250 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: 'Buy the dip, a 10% correction is a gift' is the standard long-only advice; it tests whether the drawdown level carries information beyond always being long.
source: Investopedia 'Correction'; Fidelity / Schwab 'What to do in a 10% correction' explainers; countless 'buy the dip QQQ' threads

name: Buy the dip in a bull market: 10% off the 20-day high while above the 200-day SMA, exit on a new 20-day high or trend break (crypto)
rule: s200 = ctx.sma('close',200); h20 = max(close over i-20..i-1). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > s200[i] AND close[i] <= 0.90*h20. EXIT when close[i] > max(close over i-20..i-1) (new 20-day closing high) OR close[i] < s200[i] OR 30 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Bull-market dips in crypto are bought aggressively by the same crowd that sold them; a 10% pullback inside a 200-day uptrend is the textbook retail entry.
source: r/CryptoCurrency 'buy the dip' canon; Investopedia 'Buy the Dips'; Benjamin Cowen 'bull market corrections' videos

name: Three red days above the 200-day: buy after three consecutive down closes, sell on the first up close (equity ETFs)
rule: ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] < close[i-1] AND close[i-1] < close[i-2] AND close[i-2] < close[i-3] AND close[i] > ctx.sma('close',200,i). EXIT when close[i] > close[i-1] (first green close) OR 10 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Short-term index reversal after consecutive down days is the most searched 'buy the dip' timing rule on QQQ; the 200-day filter is how retail is told to apply it.
source: Larry Connors, How Markets Really Work (2004), 'consecutive down days'; YouTube 'three red candles strategy'

name: Three red days above the 200-day on crypto: buy after three consecutive down closes, sell on the first up close
rule: ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] < close[i-1] AND close[i-1] < close[i-2] AND close[i-2] < close[i-3] AND close[i] > ctx.sma('close',200,i). EXIT when close[i] > close[i-1] OR 5 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Same question as the ETF version on the asset where 'buy the dip after 3 red days' is actually most repeated (BTC/alts); crypto daily autocorrelation is weaker so it may not transfer.
source: Larry Connors, How Markets Really Work (2004); crypto Twitter/TikTok '3 red days then green' posts

name: RSI(14) above 70 as a momentum buy on US stocks: enter on the cross above 70, exit below 50
rule: r = ctx.rsi(14). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND r[i] >= 70 AND r[i-1] < 70. EXIT when r[i] < 50. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The 'RSI above 70 is strength, not a sell' argument (Cardwell) versus the textbook overbought rule; tested on crypto already, here on the large caps beginners trade.
source: Andrew Cardwell RSI seminars (1990s); Constance Brown, Technical Analysis for the Trading Professional (1999); Investopedia 'RSI'

name: Buy last week's winners: top 5 of 40 large caps by 1-week return, rebalanced weekly
rule: rank(universe, t): for each symbol with >= 6 bars, score = close[t]/close[t-5]-1. Hold the top 5 by score at equal weight (0.2 each); all others 0. Rebalance weekly. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Beginners buy whatever rose last week; the academic prior is short-term reversal, but the direct 'top gainers of the week' book has not been scored on these names.
source: Jegadeesh (1990) and Lehmann (1990) for the weekly reversal prior; retail 'top gainers' screens on Yahoo Finance / Robinhood

name: 10% trailing stop on buy-and-hold with re-entry on a new 20-day closing high
rule: Start long on the first bar with 21 bars of history. While long: peak = max close since entry (including the entry close); EXIT when close[i] <= 0.90*peak. While flat: ENTER long at close of bar i when close[i] > max(close over i-20..i-1). Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: 'Set a 10% trailing stop' is the most common beginner risk rule; Kaminski-Lo show stop-loss rules only help when returns are positively autocorrelated, so this is a direct test on large caps.
source: Kaminski & Lo, 'When do stop-loss rules stop losses?', Journal of Financial Markets (2014); Investopedia 'Trailing Stop'

name: Mayer Multiple overheat exit: long while close is below 2.4x the 200-day SMA, flat above it (crypto)
rule: mm = close[i] / ctx.sma('close',200,i). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND mm < 2.4. EXIT when mm >= 2.4. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Trace Mayer's rule: historically buying above 2.4x the 200-day average has been a poor entry; the buy-zone (<1.0) half was tested, the overheat exit was not.
source: Trace Mayer, 'Mayer Multiple' (2017), mayermultiple.info; Investopedia / LookIntoBitcoin 'Mayer Multiple'

name: YouTube MACD + 200 EMA: hourly MACD cross up below the zero line above the 200 EMA, 1.5R target, swing-low stop (crypto)
rule: e = ctx.ema('close',200); line = ctx.ema('close',12)-ctx.ema('close',26); sig = EMA(9) of line; ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND close[i] > e[i] AND line[i-1] <= sig[i-1] AND line[i] > sig[i] AND line[i] < 0. entry = close[i]; stop = min(low over i-10..i); R = entry - stop (require R > 0); target = entry + 1.5R. EXIT at the first close <= stop OR close >= target OR 48 bars after entry. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: The single most-viewed 'high win-rate' retail strategy on YouTube: pullback crosses below zero inside an uptrend; the test is whether the 1.5R bracket survives hourly crypto costs.
source: Trade Pro / 'MACD + 200 EMA strategy' videos (YouTube, 2019-2023, tens of millions of views); Investopedia 'MACD'

name: Hourly golden cross on crypto: long while the 50 EMA is above the 200 EMA
rule: f = ctx.ema('close',50); s = ctx.ema('close',200). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND f[i] > s[i]. EXIT when f[i] < s[i]. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: Retail runs the golden cross on intraday charts (1h/4h) far more than on daily; the 9/21 hourly cross was tested, the 50/200 one that defines 'trend' for most beginners was not.
source: TradingView / Binance Academy 'Golden cross on lower timeframes'; Investopedia 'Golden Cross'

name: ICT weekly open: Monday-Tuesday dip below the weekly open then reclaim, long into Thursday close, in an uptrend (hourly crypto)
rule: dow = floor(time/86400 + 4) mod 7 (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday) and hour = floor(time/3600) mod 24, both UTC from bar.time. weekOpen = open of the Monday 00:00 bar of the current week; weekLow = min low since that bar; dipped = weekLow < weekOpen. Trend: close[i] > ctx.ema('close',1200,i). ENTER long at close of bar i if flat AND dow in {1,2} AND dipped AND close[i] > weekOpen AND close[i-1] <= weekOpen AND trend AND no entry yet this week. stop = weekLow at entry. EXIT when close[i] < stop OR at the close of the Thursday (dow 4) 23:00 bar, whichever first. Long only. All decisions use bars[0..i] only; every entry and exit is taken at the close of bar i (close-based stops, no intrabar fills). Equal weight across assets, full size per asset when long.
rationale: ICT's weekly profile: in bullish weeks price runs the lows under the weekly open on Monday/Tuesday before expanding higher into Thursday; the reclaim is the published entry.
source: ICT (Michael Huddleston) 'Weekly Profiles' / 'Weekly Open' mentorship videos (YouTube 2016-2022); TradingView 'ICT weekly open' scripts
